key_insight: JEPA-Anything proposes a single predictive learning principle that can work across very different environments, instead of relying on domain-specific world models. Its core idea, orthogonal predictive factorization, splits what needs to be predicted into complementary latent factors so the model can learn them more effectively.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a general world-modeling framework: most predictive models are tailored to one domain and do not transfer well across radically different systems.
method: Extends joint-embedding predictive architectures with orthogonal predictive factorization (OPF).
Decomposes latent targets into complementary factors and assigns them to dedicated prediction pathways.
Learns a domain-agnostic predictive model that can support world modeling across diverse environments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a path toward more reusable predictive models that can generalize beyond a single task or domain. It could reduce the need to redesign world models from scratch for each new application.

paper_title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
paper_authors: Taoyong Cui, Zhongyao Wang, Xinyue Xu, Weiyang Liu, Zhaochen Yu
